title: Taiwan's president calls for Micron, workers to negotiate 'sincerely' ahead of possible strike
key_facts: President Lai Ching-te urged Micron and its unions on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 to negotiate "sincerely" ahead of a possible strike.
He spoke in Taichung at the opening of a new Micron advanced assembly and testing facility.
Last week a union won member authorisation to strike over a bonus-scheme dispute.
Micron employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan and says it has invested more than NT$1.6 trillion there.
Manish Bhatia, Micron president and chief operating officer, said 2027 capacity of the new factory is sold out and expects high-bandwidth memory to grow faster than the rest of DRAM through 2028.
The unions encourage members to take a day off on 19 Oct for a Taipei rally which they say is not a strike.
quote_evidence: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te called on Thursday for US memory chipmaker Micron Technology and its workers to negotiate "sincerely" ahead of a possible strike by the company's union in Taiwan.

"We have already sold out all the capacity for 2027 that this factory will build and we expect high-bandwidth memory to grow faster than the rest of the DRAM industry all the way through 2028," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A strike at Micron's largest hub could affect supply of memory used in AI servers.
notes: Text is wire-style but the article does not name its original agency; credited to The Edge Malaysia.
